method: The S81 die places dsfd_ctrl / dsfd_svc / dsfd_sp_capture / dsfd_bk_collector as single masters; S81-PH hardened each as tiles (physical/s81_ph_views/closed/<tile>/<tile>_{ss,tt,ff}.lib, write_timing_model ETMs of the routed tiles).  With every tile of a slab closed, the slab's die-facing timing is the tile timing: a die-facing slab pin IS a tile pin (tools/budgets/ tiles.py: "the slab pin is the tile pin", inherit, length 0), so the assembled ETM of a slab takes, per slab die port, the worst arc over every tile pin bit that implements it (setup / hold / recovery / removal: max constraint; clk->q: max delay at SS / TT, min delay at FF), tables copied verbatim (tile clock insertion is inside them: the die must NOT add the routed insertion of an assembled master again).  Tile clock pins map to the slab clock pins by name (capture's serial-clock ckv arcs map to the slab's only die clock 'ck', as the die netlist feeds the slab one clock).
